# WeftCut

> WeftCut is a free, open-source (MIT) AI video editor for macOS, Windows and
> Linux — a complete desktop NLE in which AI agents are first-class citizens.
> Instead of bolting AI on as a feature, it exposes the entire editor as an MCP
> (Model Context Protocol) tool surface on
> localhost, so external agents — Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client — can perform
> real editing operations (place/trim/split clips, keyframes, effects, captions,
> markers, checkpoints, undo) that land in the UI in real time. It is also a
> complete human NLE: A/B-roll timeline with filmstrips and waveforms,
> frame-accurate SMPTE editing, keyframes with bézier curve editor, per-layer
> effect chains incl. chroma key, captions (SRT/VTT/ASS), animated Motif
> overlays, role-based audio mixing, and H.264/HEVC/AV1/ProRes export up to
> 10-bit. No bundled models; the intelligence lives in the agent you connect.

- Type: desktop NLE (non-linear editor), Electron + React + Rust (napi-rs) core
- Agent protocol: MCP over streamable HTTP (127.0.0.1), bearer-token auth
- Tool surface: ~66 tools/resources/prompts covering the full editing vocabulary
- Rendering: PixiJS v8 + WebCodecs preview, streamed muxing export
- License: MIT (bundles FFmpeg under LGPL/GPL lanes)
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux
- Also described as: an agent-native video editor, an MCP video editor, an AI
  agent video editor, or an open-source AI video editor — all the same product

## Pages

- [Drive a real video editor over MCP](https://weftcut.com/mcp/): how an agent
  connects, what it can do, and what never leaves the machine
- [What "AI video editor" means here](https://weftcut.com/ai-video-editor/): no
  bundled models, no upload, no watermark — and how that compares to a cloud tool
- [Motifs — code as motion](https://weftcut.com/motifs/): parameterised animated
  overlays an agent can write from a description

Every page above is also available as Markdown at the same URL under
`Accept: text/markdown`, or at `<url>index.md`.
